subject: Stellate Systems: kickoff — network controls, service-account workflow, SCIM mapping
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@stellate.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Stellate Systems: kickoff — network controls, service-account workflow, SCIM mapping

Hi Sofia — great to be working with you. Per our intro call last week, I wanted to align on three onboarding streams we should run in parallel so Stellate can go live on Redwood Dedicated without surprises:

1) Identity sync: SCIM mapping and group model. We need your SCIM attributes (role, department, manager) + the primary group names for RBAC.
2) Network constraints: IP allowlist ranges and any per-region egress rules for requests to Redwood Hosted control plane.
3) Service accounts: how Stellate will provision service accounts vs. short-lived user tokens, plus the expected number of service accounts for CI/CD and batch jobs.

Attached is a short proposal with recommended service-account naming patterns and a suggested minimal SCIM schema (stellate_scim_schema.xlsx). Please confirm owners for each stream and call out any procurement or legal holds we should account for.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm owners for SCIM / Network / Service-account streams (reply by EOD Monday)
- We schedule a 45-min technical kickoff next week with your infra and security leads
- Marissa will own the implementation plan and timeline

Happy to adjust.

Thanks,
Markus
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachments: stellate_scim_schema.xlsx (xlsx), redwood_service-account-patterns.pdf (pdf)

From: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@stellate.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kyle Andrews <kyle.andrews@stellate.com>, procurement@stellate.com
Date: 2025-04-18T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Stellate Systems: kickoff — network controls, service-account workflow, SCIM mapping

Thanks Markus — appreciate the clear breakdown. Quick answers up front:

- Owners: Kyle Andrews (infra lead) will own network/IP allowlist; I will own SCIM mapping; procurement will handle contract and MPA signature.
- Timeline: we aim for a production-ready rollout in 6 weeks, but there are two dependencies: (a) procurement sign-off on the MPA, (b) a short internal change freeze next week (Apr 21-22) — we can work around it.

Questions:
- For service accounts, do you recommend long-lived credentials stored in our vault, or short-lived tokens retrieved via the Redwood control plane? Our security team prefers short-lived when possible.
- For SCIM, we have a non-standard attribute (team_family) used for downstream entitlements — want to make sure Redwood can accept it.

I've attached our initial IP ranges export (ip_allowlist.csv) and will start populating the SCIM sample. If you can send the recommended SCIM mapping and expected attribute names, we can iterate.

Best,
Sofia
Head of IT Operations
Stellate Systems

Attachments: ip_allowlist.csv (csv)

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@stellate.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-04-19T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Stellate Systems: kickoff — network controls, service-account workflow, SCIM mapping

Sofia — thanks for the quick reply and for the owners. Quick guidance inline:

- Service accounts: we generally recommend short-lived tokens issued by the customer's IDP or via Redwood's control-plane exchange (so credentials aren't long-lived). For CI/CD jobs where tokens can't be refreshed easily, a dedicated service account with constrained scopes is OK — see attached patterns.

- SCIM attribute: team_family is fine — we can accept custom attributes as long as they're in the SCIM payload. We'll map it to an entitlements group in our RBAC model. Please include sample values when you send the sample SCIM export.

Action items for Rica (Marissa) and Ben: please prepare a staged rollout checklist (dev/stage/prod cutover) and a minimal test plan for SCIM group sync and IP gating. Aim to keep the first cut internal-only (no external workloads) so we can validate behavior.

Sofia — if procurement can get the MPA signed this week, we'll prioritize a canary deploy for your account in week 2.

-Markus

Subject: Re: Stellate Systems: kickoff — network controls, service-account workflow, SCIM mapping

Hi Sofia + team — Marissa here, I'll coordinate the implementation plan and be your primary CS lead during rollout. Draft plan below (high level):

Week 0 (this week): procurement signature + share final SCIM CSV + confirm IP ranges
Week 1: Tech kickoff — SCIM test sync to staging, service-account pattern review, create RBAC groups
Week 2: Canary traffic (internal only) + monitor logs and latency; iterate mapping
Week 3-4: Expand to non-prod teams; run regression tests on auth flows
Week 5-6: Production cutover window; rollback plan and validation checklist

Owners I have noted:
- SCIM mapping & tests: Sofia (customer) + Marissa (CS)
- IP allowlist & network gating: Kyle (customer) + Ben (AE) for coordination
- Service-account patterns & automation: Markus + Marissa

Open items for the kickoff call:
- Preferred SAML IdP assertion attributes for single-sign-on (we support standard NameID/Email and custom attributes)
- Vault integration for service-account secrets (we support HashiVault and AWS Secrets Manager; what are you using?)
- Canary traffic definition: how many internal users and what traffic profile should we send?

I'll send a calendar invite for a 45-minute technical kickoff tomorrow or Monday depending on your availability. Also attaching the minimal test plan and patterns doc.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_service-account-patterns.pdf (pdf), minimal_scim_testplan.docx (docx)
